guide.summary: Pre-Columbian and contemporary art museums, Barranco galleries and clifftop Miraflores, with tasting menus, cevicherías, bakeries and bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: MALI, MAC Lima, Museo Pedro de Osma and LUM all list Tuesday-to-Sunday hours and are closed on Mondays, so make Monday your Museo Larco day, since it says it opens every day, including holidays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: MALI, MAC Lima, Museo Pedro de Osma and LUM publish Tuesday-to-Sunday hours, so they are closed on Mondays. Museo Larco says it opens every day, including holidays, from 9am to 7pm.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Museo Larco charges S/ 50 general admission and says buying online gives a special discount and preferential access. LUM's own site says entry is free with a DNI (Peru's national ID).

toolkit.label: Restaurant booking
toolkit.copy: Maido releases reservations two months in advance on the first day of each month, online for 1 to 10 people, and is closed on Sundays. Central lists lunch and dinner sittings Monday to Saturday only.

toolkit.label: House rules
toolkit.copy: Café del Museo Larco does not allow pets, outside food such as cakes, or decorations, and charges S/ 60 corkage per bottle of wine. Groups of more than six are seated once 70% of the party has arrived.

guide.dek: Plan museums for Tuesday to Sunday, keep Monday for Museo Larco, and book tasting menus such as Maido well before you fly.
intro: This guide is built around places that publish their own schedules. Museo Larco in Pueblo Libre says it opens every day, including holidays, from 9am to 7pm, with general admission at S/ 50 and a discount plus preferential access when you buy online. Its Café del Museo Larco serves lunch and dinner daily and opens at 9am on Sundays for brunch, though it asks you not to bring pets or outside food. In central Lima, MALI sits in the Parque de la Exposición and lists Tuesday-to-Sunday hours from 10am to 6pm, closing at 5pm on Saturdays.

Barranco rewards a slower afternoon. MAC Lima on Av. Grau is closed on Mondays and open 10am to 7pm Tuesday to Sunday, and its "Contemporáneo 1" display in Sala 3 runs until 31 December 2026. A short walk away, Museo Pedro de Osma opens Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm and offers S/ 10 entry on the first Sunday of the month for Peruvians and residents only. In Miraflores, LUM (Lugar de la Memoria) on Bajada San Martín is free with a DNI and shows Erika Humala's "Sobreviviendo en azul y tierra" until 15 February 2027.

For tasting menus, book early. Maido, at Calle San Martín 399 in Miraflores, releases reservations two months ahead on the first day of each month and serves Monday to Saturday only. Central, on Av. Pedro de Osma in Barranco, lists lunch and dinner sittings Monday to Saturday. For a simpler seafood lunch, La Mar on Av. La Mar keeps daytime hours, closing at 5pm Monday to Thursday, while Pescados Capitales, further along Av. Mariscal La Mar, serves until 11pm Monday to Saturday. Chifa Titi in San Isidro is closed on Mondays.

Mornings can start at El Pan de la Chola on Av. Mariscal La Mar, whose Pan & Café branch lists daily hours from 7am to 9pm, or at Isolina in Barranco, which serves breakfast from 9am to 11am on Saturdays and Sundays. For an evening drink, Hotel B in Barranco describes a ground-floor bar beside reception, and Belmond Miraflores Park lists Belo Bar among its venues. Ayahuasca Restobar on Av. San Martín in Barranco publishes late hours, but on a page last dated 2023, so check before you go.
summaryCards: Pair Museo Larco, open every day, with MALI or MAC Lima, remembering that MALI, MAC Lima, Museo Pedro de Osma and LUM are closed on Mondays.
Start with Sunday brunch at Café del Museo Larco from 9am, or a weekend breakfast at Isolina in Barranco, served 9am to 11am on Saturdays and Sundays.
Maido opens reservations two months ahead on the first day of each month, and both Maido and Central list Monday-to-Saturday service only.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The input guide contained only generic entries, so every place here was added and checked separately. Several confirmed places publish hours only on undated or older pages: Museo Amano (copyright 2021), Museo Oro del Perú (2018), Restaurante Huaca Pucllana (2020), Ayahuasca Restobar (2023), El Chinito (2025) and Pastelería San Antonio (latest dates 2024–2025); Hotel B, Cosme and Larcomar pages are undated, and Larcomar, Rafael, El Mercado, El Chinito and Belmond Miraflores Park publish no regular hours. MALI lists exhibitions by single dates, not ranges, so run lengths are unclear. Kjolle's booking page says "Reservas disponibles hasta finales de Octubre", so it is left out of the guide lists until the position after October is clear. Sites that could not be read include MATE (connection refused), Circuito Mágico del Agua (TLS error), Parque de las Leyendas (HTTP 418), Museo Central (bot check), Casa de la Literatura and Country Club Lima Hotel (HTTP 403), Puku Puku and La Rosa Náutica (HTTP 429), and Gran Hotel Bolívar (SSL error). Casa de Aliaga's site carries unrelated gambling links, and the Museo Andrés del Castillo and Convento de San Francisco catacomb domains redirect to unrelated sites. Astrid y Gastón, Mayta, Panchita, Tanta and ChocoMuseo publish no usable address on the pages read.
